messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novawellness.com>

Subject: URGENT: 18% request failures and long tail latency during promo burst

Diego —

We started a marketing push at 08:45 PT this morning and immediately saw a spike of 429s and request timeouts hitting our integration with Redwood. Our app logs show ~18% of generation calls returned 429/503 or never completed (timed out). Latency tail increased from ~120ms median to 2.1s P99. This is customer-facing (checkout flow) and revenue-impacting.

Attached: screenshot-429s.png and nova-cust-traffic-sample.log (sample request IDs included).

Have you seen this pattern before? Can you scope what changed and advise an immediate mitigation? We need a short blameless postmortem and a fix ASAP; can join a call if helpful.

Thanks —
Samira Khan
Director, Integrations
NOVA Health

Subject: Re: URGENT: 18% request failures and long tail latency during promo burst

Samira —

Thanks for the samples and for flagging this so quickly. We're investigating now. Immediate notes:
- I see error spikes correlated with short burst windows in our telemetry for your tenant (NOV A).
- Quick mitigation I'm pushing now: temporarily increase your burst capacity and extend the burst decay window so tokens don't drain prematurely. This should reduce immediate 429s within minutes.

Can you confirm the sample request IDs you attached (nova-req-7a2f, nova-req-7a33) are representative? We'll also need a 30-minute window to watch traffic after the change.

I've attached a short mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_v1.docx) that lists steps and ownership. I'll loop in infra (Jonas) for deeper RCA and will keep you posted. If you're free, let's do a 10-30 min bridge at 10:15 PT.

— Diego
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Laura —

Forwarding a customer P1: NOVA Health is seeing sustained 429s (peak ~18%) during a short marketing burst. I performed an initial mitigation (temporary burst_capacity increase + extended decay) and requested a short bridge. Jonas is onboard for RCA.

Why I need exec visibility: NOVA has an SLO and this is revenue-impacting during a campaign. We will need:
- Authorization for a temporary org-wide policy override for NOVA if infra confirms the need (I recommend yes for 3 hours)
- Communication ok to the customer that we performed an emergency override (we should avoid legal-sounding wording)

Impact snapshot (pre-mitigation): 08:45–09:10 PT — 18% error rate, 2.1s P99, ~4500 requests dropped.
Proposed immediate course:
1) Approve temporary policy override (increase burst_capacity x3 and set decay window to 600s)
2) Jonas and infra to PR a validation patch to guard against zero-value decay intervals (root suspect)
3) Postmortem and customer-facing summary within 48 hours

I'd like a yes/no in 30 minutes so I can proceed with the full mitigation if infra confirms.

— Diego

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 13:20:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: 18% request failures and long tail latency during promo burst — exec note and ask

Team —

Preliminary RCA from infra: root cause is a policy misconfiguration in the tenant-specific rate governor. Specifically:
- The token-bucket safety-valve (burst_credit_decay_interval) for NOVA was set to 0s due to a config merge bug during a recent rollout of dynamic per-tenant policies.
- A 0s decay interval causes the bucket to be treated as non-refilling for the duration of the burst evaluation path, effectively draining burst credits on first large request waves and blocking refills.
- The checks were permissive, so the orchestration accepted the 0 value without fallback.

Immediate recommended actions (already implemented as of 12:50 PT):
1) Reapply safe defaults: set burst_credit_decay_interval = 600s for NOVA and restore burst_capacity = baseline * 3 (temporary).
2) Deploy a validation gate that rejects zero/negative decay intervals at policy ingest.
3) Add a short-term metric and alert: tenant_burst_refill_rate < 0.01 triggers PagerDuty P1.

Estimated customer impact (based on logs): ~4.5k requests dropped, percent failures fell to <1% within 18 minutes of the temporary config change. We'll revert temporary capacity after 3 hours and ensure config validation is in place before rolling other changes.

I'll open INF-4721 with a patch and schedule a canary for the validation gate.

— Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novawellness.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@novawellness.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RESOLVED: NOVA promo burst — drop rate mitigated, next steps

Samira / Tom —

Update and quick summary:
- We identified a tenant policy ingest bug that allowed a zero-value burst_credit_decay_interval for NOVA.
- Mitigation performed: temporary burst_capacity increase x3 and burst_credit_decay_interval set to 600s at 12:50 PT on Thu.
- Result: error rate dropped from ~18% to 0.5% within 18 minutes; P99 latency returned to normal. We observed ~4.5k requests that failed during the window.

What we did for you:
1) Immediate mitigation (temporary capacity and decay window) — completed and validated.
2) Infra patch scheduled (INF-4721) to reject zero/negative decay interval values at policy ingest — ETA 24 hours for canary, 72 hours for full rollout.
3) Postmortem and customer-facing summary in progress — link will be shared when ready.

Next steps for NOVA (action items):
- We will follow up with a short remediation summary and an offer to run a controlled replay for requests dropped during the window (to minimize customer-facing risk).
- Jonas will confirm when INF-4721 is canaried; we'll then safely revert the temporary capacity change.

Apologies for the disruption. Thank you for the quick signals and logs — they made the RCA much faster. Please reply if you want a detailed timeline or are available for a short postmortem call next week.

Best —
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
